title: History of Jerusalem
content: Jerusalem is one of the oldest cities in the world, with a history spanning over 5,000 years. It is sacred to Judaism, Christianity, and Islam. The Old City contains the Western Wall, Church of the Holy Sepulchre, and Al-Aqsa Mosque within its ancient walls.
summary: 5,000 years of history in the holy city

title: Understanding Shabbat
content: Shabbat (Sabbath) begins Friday at sunset and ends Saturday night. Most businesses close, public transport stops in many cities. Restaurants may close or operate with limited service. Plan ahead for Shabbat, especially in Jerusalem.
summary: Essential guide to the Jewish day of rest

title: Israeli Cuisine Guide
content: Israeli cuisine is a melting pot of flavors from Middle Eastern, Mediterranean, and global influences. Must-try dishes include hummus, falafel, shakshuka, sabich, and fresh salads. Street food culture is vibrant in cities like Tel Aviv and Jerusalem.
summary: A culinary journey through Israel's diverse flavors

title: Dead Sea: Nature's Wonder
content: The Dead Sea is the lowest point on Earth at 430m below sea level. Its mineral-rich waters and mud have therapeutic properties. The sea is shrinking rapidly, making it a must-visit destination. Float effortlessly due to the extreme salinity.
summary: The world's saltiest lake and natural spa

title: Getting Around Israel
content: Israel has efficient public transport including buses (Egged, Dan), trains (Israel Railways), and shared taxis (sherut). The Rav-Kav card works across all systems. Ride-sharing apps like Gett and Yango are popular. On Shabbat, most public transport stops.

title: Safety Tips for Tourists
content: Israel is generally safe for tourists. Be aware of your surroundings, follow local news, and know emergency numbers (Police: 100, Ambulance: 101). Download the Home Front Command app for rocket alerts. Most tourist areas have security presence.
summary: Stay safe during your visit to Israel

title: The Negev Desert
content: The Negev covers over half of Israel's land area. Highlights include Ramon Crater (the world's largest erosion crater), Bedouin culture, ancient Nabatean cities, and stunning stargazing. Best visited October-April for comfortable temperatures.

title: Tel Aviv: The White City
content: Tel Aviv has the largest collection of Bauhaus/International Style buildings in the world, earning UNESCO World Heritage status. Over 4,000 buildings from the 1930s-40s line the boulevards. The White City walking tour covers key examples.
